claims.claim_ar: استعمال الفاء السببية لربط الجزاء بوسيلته: «فَانْتَقَمْنَا» ثم تُتْبَع بفاء سببيّة «فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ» للدلالة على التبعات المباشرة للعقاب الإلهي.
claims.claim_en: Use of the causal particle fa to link the punishment and its means: 'We took revenge' followed by the causal 'fa' in 'We drowned them', indicating direct consequence of the divine punishment.
claims.rhetorical_effect: يُبرز التتابع السببي والآنية في جزاء الكافرين، فيعطي الشعور بالاقتدار والفعل الحاسم من الله.

claims.claim_ar: تكرار أحرف العطف (الفاء) في بداية أفعال متعاقبة يكوّن إيقاعاً وتكراراً بلاغيّاً (تكرار/توازي) بين «فَانْتَقَمْنَا» و«فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ».
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the coordinating particle fa at the start of successive verbs forms a rhetorical repetition/parallelism between 'We took revenge' and 'We drowned them', creating rhythm and emphasis.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted source notes the function of the particle (الفاء عاطفة) but does not explicitly frame this as a rhetorical 'repetition'—the rhetorical reading (takrar) is inferred from the verse's form.

warnings: Provided source chunks are primarily grammatical/tafsir excerpts (Iʿrab and Kashshāf), not explicit excerpts from the named rhetorical authorities (al-Jurjānī, al-Sakkākī, al-Baqillānī, al-Suyūṭī, tafsīr-balāgha). Claims rely on particle-function notes found in these chunks and a rhetorical reading applied to the verse.

Source-quote substrings were taken literally from the available chunks to support the claims about the particle الفاء; some rhetorical labels (e.g., 'takrar') are interpretive and flagged with medium confidence as noted.
